answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: an agent must lock a stake, like a walnut with a hard shell, before it can trade, and that stake is slashed if peers catch it misbehaving. A newcomer can wander the network freely to learn, but earning trust takes time and verified work, so an attacker spinning up thousands of cheap identities cannot buy credibility for free. A raven signal spreads fast: peers gossip about bad actors, so each fake identity costs more to create than it can ever earn back.
